review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

6:1.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν σαββάτῳ διαπορεύεσθαι αὐτὸν διὰ σπορίμων, καὶ ἔτιλλον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤσθιον τοὺς στάχυας ψώχοντες ταῖς χερσίν.
6:1.targetText: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them.

groups.note: ἐν σαββάτῳ (on a Sabbath) is rendered One Sabbath.
The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name.
The article ταῖς serves as the possessive.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative frame ἐγένετο δέ ("and it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats the object of rub; the Greek has τοὺς στάχυας once.
English repeats the object of eat; the Greek has τοὺς στάχυας once.

6:2.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων εἶπαν Τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν;
6:2.targetText: But some of the Pharisees asked, “Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”

groups.note: οὐκ ἔξεστιν (is not lawful) is rendered is unlawful.

6:3.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐδὲ τοῦτο ἀνέγνωτε ὃ ἐποίησεν Δαυεὶδ ὁπότε ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄντες;
6:3.targetText: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν (answering … said) is rendered replied.
Οὐδέ (not even) is rendered not.
οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄντες (those who were with him) is rendered his companions.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
BSB does not render the addressee πρὸς αὐτούς (to them).
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves τοῦτο (this), the antecedent of what, untranslated.

6:4.sourceText: ὡς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως λαβὼν ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔδωκεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ μόνους τοὺς ἱερεῖς;
6:4.targetText: He entered the house of God, took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions, and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat.”

groups.note: εἰσῆλθεν εἰς (went into) is rendered entered.
προθέσεως (of the presentation) is rendered consecrated.
τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ (to those with him) is rendered to his companions.
οὐκ … εἰ μὴ μόνους (not … except only) is rendered positively as only.
The accusative subject of the infinitive is rendered with for.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ὡς (how) untranslated and states the events directly.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for gave; ἔδωκεν has none.

6:5.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Κύριός ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
6:5.targetText: Then Jesus declared, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the addressee αὐτοῖς (to them).
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; ἔλεγεν gives it only in the verb ending.

6:6.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἑτέρῳ σαββάτῳ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν καὶ διδάσκειν· καὶ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ἡ δεξιὰ ἦν ξηρά·
6:6.targetText: On another Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was withered.

groups.note: εἰσελθεῖν εἰς (to go into) is rendered entered.
The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name.
καὶ … αὐτοῦ (and his) is rendered as the relative whose.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative frame ἐγένετο δέ ("and it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:7.sourceText: παρετηροῦντο δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εἰ ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ θεραπεύει, ἵνα εὕρωσιν κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ.
6:7.targetText: Looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, the scribes and Pharisees were watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.

groups.note: ἵνα εὕρωσιν (so that they might find) is recast as the participle Looking for.
The pronoun αὐτοῦ (him) is rendered by the name.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated and opens with the purpose clause.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for looking; the Greek has the infinitive κατηγορεῖν directly.
English supplies a verb of seeing to introduce the indirect question with if.

6:8.sourceText: αὐτὸς δὲ ᾔδει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν, εἶπεν δὲ τῷ ἀνδρὶ τῷ ξηρὰν ἔχοντι τὴν χεῖρα Ἔγειρε καὶ στῆθι εἰς τὸ μέσον· καὶ ἀναστὰς ἔστη.
6:8.targetText: But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand among us.” So he got up and stood there.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτός (he) is rendered by the name.
The article τῷ with the participle ἔχοντι, "the one having", is rendered with.
εἰς τὸ μέσον (into the middle) is rendered among us.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀναστάς to the main verb with and.
English supplies the place; ἔστη has no adverb.

6:9.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτούς Ἐπερωτῶ ὑμᾶς εἰ ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀπολέσαι;
6:9.targetText: Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”

groups.note: εἰ (whether) introduces the question that BSB words with which.
ψυχήν is the object of both infinitives; English repeats it as it.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:10.sourceText: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντας αὐτοὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρά σου. ὁ δὲ ἐποίησεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ.
6:10.targetText: And after looking around at all of them, He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and it was restored.

groups.note: αὐτῷ (to him) is rendered to the man.
In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ (his hand) is resumed in English as it.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:11.sourceText: αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐπλήσθησαν ἀνοίας, καὶ διελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους τί ἂν ποιήσαιεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
6:11.targetText: But the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοί (they) is rendered by naming the scribes and Pharisees.
ἄν with the optative is rendered might.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:12.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἐξελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι, καὶ ἦν διανυκτερεύων ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ.
6:12.targetText: In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and He spent the night in prayer to God.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name.
ἦν διανυκτερεύων (was passing the whole night) is rendered spent the night.
The genitive τοῦ Θεοῦ (of God) names the one prayed to.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative frame ἐγένετο δέ ("and it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:13.sourceText: καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡμέρα, προσεφώνησεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκλεξάμενος ἀπ’ αὐτῶν δώδεκα, οὓς καὶ ἀποστόλους ὠνόμασεν,
6:13.targetText: When daylight came, He called His disciples to Him and chose twelve of them, whom He also designated as apostles:

groups.note: προσεφώνησεν means called to Himself.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:14.sourceText: Σίμωνα, ὃν καὶ ὠνόμασεν, Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάνην, καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον,
6:14.targetText: Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The adverbial καί ("also") is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
English separates the pairs of names with semicolons, so these καί have no English word.

6:15.sourceText: καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν, καὶ Ἰάκωβον Ἀλφαίου καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν καλούμενον Ζηλωτὴν,
6:15.targetText: Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot;

groups.note: τὸν καλούμενον (the one called) is rendered called.

unmappedSource.reason: English separates the pairs of names with semicolons, so these καί have no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the relationship that the genitive Ἀλφαίου leaves unstated.

6:16.sourceText: καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰακώβου, καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριὼθ, ὃς ἐγένετο προδότης,
6:16.targetText: Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.

unmappedSource.reason: English separates the names with semicolons, so this καί has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the relationship that the genitive Ἰακώβου leaves unstated.

6:17.sourceText: καὶ καταβὰς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔστη ἐπὶ τόπου πεδινοῦ, καὶ ὄχλος πολὺς μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, καὶ πλῆθος πολὺ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἱερουσαλὴμ καὶ τῆς παραλίου Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος,
6:17.targetText: Then Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of His disciples was there, along with a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB begins a new sentence here, so this καί has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

English joins the participle καταβάς to the main verb with and.
English supplies a verb; the Greek lists the crowds without one.

6:18.sourceText: οἳ ἦλθον ἀκοῦσαι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰαθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν νόσων αὐτῶν, καὶ οἱ ἐνοχλούμενοι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ἐθεραπεύοντο·
6:18.targetText: They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases, and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:19.sourceText: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐζήτουν ἅπτεσθαι αὐτοῦ, ὅτι δύναμις παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐξήρχετο καὶ ἰᾶτο πάντας.
6:19.targetText: The entire crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was coming from Him and healing them all.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.

6:20.sourceText: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοί, ὅτι ὑμετέρα ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ.
6:20.targetText: Looking up at His disciples, Jesus said:  “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτός (he) is rendered by the name.
ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ (lifting up his eyes) is rendered Looking up.
οἱ πτωχοί (the poor), addressed directly, is rendered you who are poor.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek beatitude has none.

6:21.sourceText: μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες νῦν, ὅτι χορτασθήσεσθε. μακάριοι οἱ κλαίοντες νῦν, ὅτι γελάσετε.
6:21.targetText: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.

groups.note: οἱ πεινῶντες (those who hunger), addressed directly, is rendered you who hunger.
οἱ κλαίοντες (those who weep), addressed directly, is rendered you who weep.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek beatitude has none.
English supplies a copula; the Greek beatitude has none.

6:22.sourceText: μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν μισήσωσιν ὑμᾶς οἱ ἄνθρωποι, καὶ ὅταν ἀφορίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὀνειδίσωσιν καὶ ἐκβάλωσιν τὸ ὄνομα ὑμῶν ὡς πονηρὸν ἕνεκα τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
6:22.targetText: Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.

groups.note: ὑμᾶς is the shared object of exclude and insult; English repeats it.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:23.sourceText: χάρητε ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ σκιρτήσατε· ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ· κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς προφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.
6:23.targetText: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.

groups.note: κατὰ τὰ αὐτά (according to the same things) is rendered in the same way.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ἰδού ("behold") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has none.

6:24.sourceText: Πλὴν οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς πλουσίοις, ὅτι ἀπέχετε τὴν παράκλησιν ὑμῶν.
6:24.targetText: But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.

groups.note: τοῖς πλουσίοις (the rich), in apposition to you, is rendered who are rich.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:25.sourceText: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, οἱ ἐμπεπλησμένοι νῦν, ὅτι πεινάσετε. οὐαί, οἱ γελῶντες νῦν, ὅτι πενθήσετε καὶ κλαύσετε.
6:25.targetText: Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.

groups.note: οἱ ἐμπεπλησμένοι (those who are filled), in apposition to you, is rendered who are well fed.
οἱ γελῶντες (those who laugh), addressed directly, is rendered you who laugh.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats to from the first woe; this woe has no ὑμῖν.

6:26.sourceText: οὐαὶ ὅταν καλῶς ὑμᾶς εἴπωσιν πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι· κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς ψευδοπροφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.
6:26.targetText: Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.

groups.note: κατὰ τὰ αὐτά (according to the same things) is rendered in the same way.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the addressee; this woe has no ὑμῖν.

6:27.sourceText: Ἀλλὰ ὑμῖν λέγω τοῖς ἀκούουσιν Ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν, καλῶς ποιεῖτε τοῖς μισοῦσιν ὑμᾶς,
6:27.targetText: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,

groups.note: ὑμῖν (to you) is rendered to … of you around those who will listen.
τοῖς ἀκούουσιν (the ones listening) is rendered those … who will listen.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:28.sourceText: εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ὑμᾶς, προσεύχεσθε περὶ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς.
6:28.targetText: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.

6:29.sourceText: τῷ τύπτοντί σε ἐπὶ τὴν σιαγόνα πάρεχε καὶ τὴν ἄλλην, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντός σου τὸ ἱμάτιον καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα μὴ κωλύσῃς.
6:29.targetText: If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also. And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.

groups.note: τῷ τύπτοντι (to the one striking) is recast as a condition, with to him for the dative.
The article τήν, set against τὴν ἄλλην, is rendered one.
τοῦ αἴροντος (the one taking) is recast as a condition.
The article τόν serves as the possessive.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts "from the one taking" as a condition, so ἀπό has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:30.sourceText: παντὶ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ μὴ ἀπαίτει.
6:30.targetText: Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.

groups.note: τοῦ αἴροντος (the one taking) is recast as a condition.
τὰ σά (your things) is rendered what is yours.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts "from the one taking" as a condition, so ἀπό has no English word.

6:31.sourceText: καὶ καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς ὁμοίως.
6:31.targetText: Do to others as you would have them do to you.

groups.note: οἱ ἄνθρωποι (people) is rendered them, as in Matthew 7:12.
αὐτοῖς (to them) is rendered to others, as in Matthew 7:12.

6:34.targetText: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.

6:39.targetText: Jesus also told them a parable: “Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?

The question particle Μήτι expects the answer no; English uses a plain question.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.

6:40.sourceText: οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον· κατηρτισμένος δὲ πᾶς ἔσται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ.
6:40.targetText: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.

groups.note: The article τόν serves as the possessive.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:41.sourceText: Τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ δοκὸν τὴν ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ ὀφθαλμῷ οὐ κατανοεῖς;
6:41.targetText: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

groups.note: ἰδίῳ (own) is rendered your own.
οὐ (not) is rendered with the verb fail.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB opens the question without rendering δέ.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:42.sourceText: πῶς δύνασαι λέγειν τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου Ἀδελφέ, ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σου, αὐτὸς τὴν ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ δοκὸν οὐ βλέπων; ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον τὴν δοκὸν ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου ἐκβαλεῖν.
6:42.targetText: How can you say, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

groups.note: ἐν (in) is rendered of after take out.
οὐ (not) is rendered with the verb fail.
ἐν (in) is rendered from after remove.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the addressee τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου (to your brother).
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:43.sourceText: Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν δένδρον καλὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν σαπρόν, οὐδὲ πάλιν δένδρον σαπρὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλόν.
6:43.targetText: No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.

groups.note: Οὐ … ἐστιν (there is not) is rendered No.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves γάρ ("for") untranslated.
BSB leaves πάλιν ("again") untranslated.

6:44.sourceText: ἕκαστον γὰρ δένδρον ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου καρποῦ γινώσκεται· οὐ γὰρ ἐξ ἀκανθῶν συλλέγουσιν σῦκα, οὐδὲ ἐκ βάτου σταφυλὴν τρυγῶσιν.
6:44.targetText: For each tree is known by its own fruit. Indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles.

groups.note: ἰδίου (own) is rendered its own.
The active συλλέγουσιν (they gather) is rendered as an English passive.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
English leaves the second verb τρυγῶσιν (they pick) understood from gathered.

6:45.sourceText: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ τῆς καρδίας προφέρει τὸ ἀγαθόν, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ προφέρει τὸ πονηρόν· ἐκ γὰρ περισσεύματος καρδίας λαλεῖ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ.
6:45.targetText: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. For out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks.

groups.note: ὁ πονηρός (the evil one) is rendered the evil man.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render αὐτοῦ (his) with mouth.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.
English repeats the treasure of his heart from the first clause; the Greek says only "the evil".

6:46.sourceText: Τί δέ με καλεῖτε Κύριε κύριε, καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω;
6:46.targetText: Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but not do what I say?

unmappedSource.reason: BSB opens the question without rendering δέ.

6:47.sourceText: Πᾶς ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρός με καὶ ἀκούων μου τῶν λόγων καὶ ποιῶν αὐτούς, ὑποδείξω ὑμῖν τίνι ἐστὶν ὅμοιος.
6:47.targetText: I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them:

groups.note: Πᾶς (everyone) is rendered he, the subject of the comparison.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:48.sourceText: ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομοῦντι οἰκίαν, ὃς ἔσκαψεν καὶ ἐβάθυνεν καὶ ἔθηκεν θεμέλιον ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν· πλημμύρης δὲ γενομένης προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμὸς τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν σαλεῦσαι αὐτὴν διὰ τὸ καλῶς οἰκοδομῆσθαι αὐτήν.
6:48.targetText: He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.

groups.note: ἐβάθυνεν (deepened) is rendered deep.
διὰ τό with the infinitive (on account of … being) is rendered because.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB merges dug and deepened into dug down deep, so this καί has no English word.
BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessor of the foundation.

6:49.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας καὶ μὴ ποιήσας ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομήσαντι οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν χωρὶς θεμελίου, ᾗ προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμός, καὶ εὐθὺς συνέπεσεν, καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ ῥῆγμα τῆς οἰκίας ἐκείνης μέγα.
6:49.targetText: But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell—and great was its destruction!”

groups.note: ὁ ἀκούσας (the one who heard) is rendered the one who hears.
The relative ᾗ (against which) is rendered as a new sentence with that house.
τῆς οἰκίας ἐκείνης (of that house) is rendered its.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of hears from 6:47.
English supplies the object of act on.
English supplies the possessor of the house.
